observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x00c0b7a0 is 8b 81 20 0b 00 00, MOV EAX,[ECX + 0xb20]; the ModRM byte 81 is mod=10 disp32 reg=000, so the receiver is ECX. ECX is then destroyed by 0x00c0b7a6 XOR ECX,ECX, but that is the compare-against-zero half of a CMP ECX,[EAX + 0x60c] and not a receiver use, because the first instruction already consumed the receiver. The epilogue is a bare RET, so there is no stack argument and the caller owns cleanup.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: A full dword in EAX that is exactly 0 or exactly 1, never an arbitrary true value and never a leftover pointer. The chain is: XOR ECX,ECX zeroes the compare operand; CMP ECX,[EAX + 0x60c] sets CF when the dword is non-zero; SBB EAX,EAX with EAX holding the sub-object pointer computes EAX - EAX - CF, i.e. 0xFFFFFFFF or 0; NEG then yields 1 or 0.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00c0b7ae SBB EAX,EAX and 0x00c0b7b0 NEG EAX together overwrite all 32 bits of EAX. Consumers agree the width is meaningful: 0x00d2c164 uses MOVZX ESI,AL, 0x00ba2835 and 0x00d2c1e6 use TEST AL,AL, and 0x00d2c156 uses SETZ CL over the AL byte. Had only AL been meaningful the compiler would have emitted SETNE AL rather than the SBB/NEG pair, so the dword width is the real contract.
observed_original_abi.hidden_receiver: read once, at the first instruction only

observed_mechanics: 0x00c0b7a0: 8b 81 20 0b 00 00 - MOV EAX,[ECX + 0xb20] loads the first-level sub-object pointer; the disp32 is 0x00000b20.
0x00c0b7a6: 33 c9 - XOR ECX,ECX materialises the zero the next CMP compares against. It clobbers the receiver register, which is safe because the receiver was already consumed.

0x00c0b7a8: 3b 88 0c 06 00 00 - CMP ECX,[EAX + 0x60c] computes 0 - [sub + 0x60c] and therefore sets CF exactly when [sub + 0x60c] is non-zero under an UNSIGNED comparison. Because the left operand is a hard zero this is equivalent to a != 0 test, and the unsigned reading is what makes negative dwords true.

0x00c0b7ae: 1b c0 - SBB EAX,EAX computes EAX - EAX - CF, i.e. 0xFFFFFFFF when CF is set and 0 when clear. This is the standard branchless boolean materialisation and it deliberately destroys the sub-object pointer that was in EAX.
0x00c0b7b0: f7 d8 - NEG EAX turns 0xFFFFFFFF into 1 and leaves 0 alone, producing a full dword 0 or 1.
0x00c0b7b2: c3 - RET with no immediate, so the callee pops zero stack words.
Live memory read at 0x00c0b7a0 returns 8b81200b000033c93b880c0600001bc0f7d8c3 followed by thirteen cc bytes, confirming all six instructions and the pad.
0x00ba2830, 0x00ba2856 and 0x00ba2866 in caller 0x00ba27b0 each TEST AL,AL immediately after the call and each gate a return value of 1 or 2, so the answer is a decision predicate, not a count.

0x00d2c14f is followed by XOR ECX,ECX ; TEST AL,AL ; SETZ CL ; MOV ESI,ECX, which INVERTS the answer: 0x00d2c15f is the untaken path, while 0x00d2c164's MOVZX ESI,AL ; NEG ESI ; SBB ESI,ESI ; AND ESI,0x3 ; DEC ESI computes a 0..3 code from the direct answer. Both sites are in the same caller 0x00d2c000, so the same predicate is deliberately consumed both ways.
There is no null check on receiver+0xb20, none on the sub-object pointer, and none on the dword at +0x60c: a null sub-object faults at 0x00c0b7a8.

semantic_contract: Return 1 in the full 32-bit EAX when the dword at byte offset +0x60c of the sub-object pointed to by receiver+0xb20 is non-zero, and 0 otherwise. The test is unsigned against a hard zero, so every non-zero bit pattern including 0x80000000 and 0xffffffff is true; there is no null check on receiver+0xb20 or on the sub-object, no clamp, no default other than the zero implied by a zero field, no callee, no global read and no side effect. The value is consumed as a decision predicate: three callsites in 0x00ba27b0 test it on both objects of a pair, and 0x00d2c000 consumes it both directly and inverted.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC: the body is complete and the ABI, both offsets, the branchless polarity and the full-dword return width are all OBSERVED and corroborated by an immediate structural sibling plus 20 callsites, but the owning class and the meaning of the flag at +0x60c are not established, and that is a material element. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY: the behavioural contract is fully determined and reconstructed, and the unsigned-versus-signed distinction that the SBB/NEG chain encodes is a real semantic claim, not a structural one. The bound is named: owning type and flag meaning.
semantic_findings: The answer is a raw flag read, not a comparison against a small domain: the model test pins 0x80000000 and 0xffffffff as true, which a signed greater-than-zero reading would have called false.

The sibling 0x00c0b780 tests the same sub-object four bytes lower, so +0x608 and +0x60c are two members of a flag cluster and callers routinely consult both - 0x00ba27b0 calls 0x00c0b780 and then 0x00c0b7a0 on the same two objects.

0x00ba27b0 is a decision function returning 1, 2 or 6, and it consults the predicate on BOTH operands of a two-object comparison; that symmetry is the strongest evidence that the flag is a per-object property rather than a relationship between objects.
0x00d2c000 deliberately consumes the answer twice, once inverted via SETZ and once directly folded into a 0..3 code, so the boolean is cheap enough to be re-read at two points in one function.
The function is branchless, so it is a leaf with no path divergence and no side effect; it appears 20 times without any caller needing to defend against state changes.
The SBB/NEG pair rather than SETNE proves the dword width is contractual: the compiler only emits the two-instruction form when the full register matters.

The briefing recorded 14 callers; the live xref query returns 20 UNCONDITIONAL_CALL references, so six further callsites exist. None is a DATA reference, so the function still occupies no vtable slot.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this function? 20 live references, all UNCONDITIONAL_CALL, and no DATA reference, so it is not a vtable slot and no owner can be named.
What does the flag at sub-object+0x60c mean? Its use as a symmetric per-object decision predicate is established; its game meaning is not.
Who writes sub-object+0x60c, and who writes the +0xb20 pointer itself? No writer was found in this batch.

What is the relationship between the flag at +0x608 (tested by 0x00c0b780) and the one at +0x60c? They are independent as far as the observed code shows, but whether they are meant to be mutually exclusive is unknown.
What are the globals 0x0156c194 and 0x0156c198 that the sibling accessor 0x00c0b8e0 is compared against in 0x00ba27b0? They were not read in this batch, so no value is claimed.
Is the receiver's +0xb20 pointer guaranteed non-null at every one of the 20 callsites? The body does not check it, so a null there would fault; no caller's guarantee was established.
